name: Porsche
description: Porsche over a generic OBD-II dongle. Honest per-era scope (docs/private/porsche-research-architecture.md §7): Porsche is three cars in one badge and splits on more walls than any brand so far. The 2005-2016 Porsche-own CAN cars (911 997/987, 991.1, 981 Boxster/Cayman, Panamera 970) answer on 11-bit/500k -- engine on the standard 7E0/7E8 block is the guaranteed module (KWP service 0x21 on 997/987, UDS 22/19 on 981+); the other module IDs were never published, so this is an honest engine + best-effort driveline read, not a PIWIS/Durametric all-module walk. Cayenne 958 (92A) and Macan 95B are VW-Group MLB cars whose modules answer the VAG address block best-effort (gateway, cluster, ABS/PSM, airbag, steering, AWD, EPB) -- but Porsche runs different control-unit software, so those are candidates to verify, not guarantees. The walls: 911 996 / Boxster 986 (1997-2005) are K-line KWP2000 -- the dongle reaches the DME/Tiptronic/alarm on K1 (pin 7) for generic EOBD only, and the ABS/airbag/cluster/HVAC body modules sit on a second K-line on pin 3 the ELM327 physically cannot reach; Cayenne 955/957 (2003-2010) is a VW Touareg on TP2.0, unreachable over BLE; and MY17+ cars (Panamera 971, Cayenne 9YA, 911 992, Macan facelift, 718 later, Taycan, plus the 991.2/982 grey zone) moved deep diagnostics to DoIP over Ethernet, which no ELM327 can speak -- generic OBD-II only. The service resets are dash procedures and work on every era that has a button method, dongle or not.

panel.title: Porsche modules (OBD dongle)
panel.hint: Module scan for Porsche over the ordinary OBD dongle. Reads the VIN first, then the modules a dongle genuinely reaches on a 2005-2016 Porsche-own CAN car: the engine (DME) on the standard block, laddering UDS then KWP-over-CAN, plus a best-effort Tiptronic/PDK probe. On a Cayenne 958 / Macan (decided from the VIN) it also best-effort walks the VAG address block those MLB cars share with VW/Audi. This is an honest engine + driveline read, NOT a full PIWIS/Durametric walk: Porsche never published its per-module CAN IDs, so PSM/ABS, airbag, cluster, PASM/PDCC and body modules answer on addresses that aren't in any public table; the crown-jewel measuring values (camshaft deviation, over-rev history, electronic oil level, PDK temps) have no public DID either. The 911 996 / Boxster 986 are K-line: the dongle gets generic EOBD on the DME (pin 7) only, and their body modules are on a second K-line on pin 3 it cannot reach. Cayenne 955/957 (TP2.0) and MY17+ / Taycan (DoIP) give generic OBD only. The Service tab's dash-procedure resets work on the eras that have a button method regardless. Pick the adapter top-right, ignition ON, then scan.

actions.label: Live extras
actions.title: Porsche live extras
actions.hint: Reads the one Porsche-specific value with a published wire format -- engine oil temperature via KWP 21 32 -- captured from a single Rennlist 997.2 CAN thread (candidate scaling A-60), so verify it against the car before trusting the absolute figure. The high-value measuring values a dealer wants (camshaft deviation for the M96/M97 IMS/chain-wear check, over-rev history, electronic oil level) are read by Durametric/PIWIS but nobody published their DIDs, so they are deliberately NOT shown as guessed numbers. On a car that doesn't answer the KWP value (a UDS-era, TP2.0 or DoIP car) it falls back to a curated generic Mode-01 set.
